stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is optimized for local coding agents and features native DFlash and image input support via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
stories.author: Ola Shorinwa
bullet_points: CLAP introduces a framework for cross-embodiment action-conditioned video generation.
It overcomes the limitation of single-robot models by training on diverse, internet-scale videos from human and robotic agents.
The model aims to create zero-shot physical simulators by leveraging heterogeneous video data to learn generalizable physics.

stories.title: Token-Level Advertising
stories.author: Qi Qi
bullet_points: Proposes Latent Advertiser Mixture Auction (LAMA) to adapt advertising for generative AI.
Shifts advertising from predefined slots to a token-level mechanism embedded directly in the generation process.
Advertisers influence the AI's output by reporting local continuation values to induce specific next-token policies.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key ML/NLP tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates active community interest and performance tracking for a major LLM model.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a substantial developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when running through Ollama 0.31.
The speed improvement is achieved by utilizing Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
The optimization results in up to 90% faster performance, particularly when integrated with coding agents.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model designed for advanced AI tasks.
The model is specifically optimized for high-throughput reasoning capabilities.
It is engineered to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these personal AI agents entirely on local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing AI workloads for Apple hardware.
This is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: Google further buries search results under AI mode
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google is automatically expanding its AI search summaries (AI Overviews) on search results pages.
This expansion pushes traditional organic search links further down the results page.
The change represents a significant shift in Google's search interface prioritizing generative AI content.

stories.title: Anthropic was illegally blacklisted by the Trump administration, court rules
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: A court ruled that the Pentagon's blacklisting of AI company Anthropic by the Trump administration was unconstitutional.
The lawsuit alleged unlawful retaliation against Anthropic by the Trump administration.
The ruling marks a significant legal victory for the AI lab in a protracted legal battle.

stories.title: Trump blacklisting of "woke" Anthropic deemed illegal by federal judge
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A federal judge ruled that Trump's blacklisting of Anthropic was illegal.
Anthropic has publicly opposed the development of lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance technologies.
The ruling highlights legal challenges against government actions targeting AI companies based on their ethical stances.

stories.title: Authorities arrest 2 alleged members of prolific hacking group TeamPCP
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Authorities have arrested two alleged members of the hacking group TeamPCP.
TeamPCP conducted a large-scale, relentless supply-chain attack campaign.
The group successfully infected over 1,000 organizations.

stories.title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
stories.author: Haoliang Li
bullet_points: Introduces RedEvoAgent, an automatic red-teaming agent designed to evolve its skills based on experience.
Highlights the increased risk posed by LLM agents in production environments due to potential harmful tool use and state changes, beyond simple text generation.
Addresses limitations in current automatic red-teaming, specifically the issues of fixed attacks and retrieval bias in trajectory-based methods.

stories.title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit
stories.author: Yisen Xi
bullet_points: Introduces Persona-Execution Separation (PES) as an architectural pattern for LLM agents.
Addresses the conflict between allowing LLM personas to evolve freely and maintaining traceable, auditable execution.
Proposes separating persona (in a mutable trust domain) from execution (in an audited, faceless domain) via a governed contract bridge.

stories.title: CorporateBench: Large-Scale Q&A Benchmarking with Temporal Knowledge Bases
stories.author: Igor Labutov
bullet_points: Introduces CorporateBench (CB), a large-scale, human-validated Q&A benchmark designed for enterprise-scale document collections.
Addresses the critical evaluation gap in LLMs by providing a realistic benchmark that avoids the privacy issues of internal corporate data.
Evaluates LLMs across multiple tasks using a corpus exceeding 230,000 documents, simulating real-world corporate communication complexity.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now supported via llama.cpp integration.
The update expands model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Xbox CEO calls Project Helix a ‘family of devices’
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma redefined 'Project Helix' from a singular console to a 'family of devices'.
This suggests Microsoft's next-generation gaming hardware will be a multi-device ecosystem.
The shift in terminology indicates a broader, more integrated hardware strategy for Xbox.

stories.title: Trump’s EPA wants to let data centers hide their air pollution
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: The EPA is planning to remove a federal rule requiring public notice for certain industrial sites.
This change specifically impacts data centers, allowing them potentially to hide air pollution.
The move comes amid growing community backlash against the environmental impact of new data centers.

stories.title: DLSS 5 leaked and modders are putting Nvidia’s AI effects on everything
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: An unofficial version of Nvidia's DLSS 5 has been leaked and is being tested by modders.
The leaked code was reportedly found in an early-access build of NBA 2K27.
Modders are applying the AI upscaling technology to popular games like Skyrim and Cyberpunk 2077.

stories.title: Meta makes AI glasses slightly less creepy with limit on nonconsensual recording
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta has updated its AI glasses software to address privacy concerns.
The update prevents the glasses from recording when the user covers the safety light.
This change aims to mitigate the risk of nonconsensual recording by the device.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile specialized knowledge and workflows from AI agent experience into reusable skills.
It addresses the limitation where insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories, hindering systematic reuse.
The system enables AI agents to progressively adapt and evolve their capabilities through continuous interaction by persisting learned skills.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM training for software engineering: relying solely on successful agent trajectories for Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) introduces noisy supervision.
The core problem identified is that successful trajectories may still contain ineffective, redundant, or risky steps, which can degrade model quality.
The proposed method, SWE-Prime, aims to improve LLM performance on real-world software issues by addressing the quality of the training data, rather than just the quantity.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: Current LLM-based code review approaches often treat the process as a single, static decision.
Real-world code review is inherently iterative and interactive, involving multiple rounds of feedback.
The research introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark LLMs against the complex, multi-round nature of realistic code review.

stories.title: Mechanistic Reaction Prediction via Discrete Flow Matching on Graph-Structured Electron Occupation
stories.author: Philippe Schwaller
bullet_points: Introduces MAELLE, a new method for predicting chemical reactions.
MAELLE models reactions not by generating molecules or editing topology, but by using discrete flow matching on electron occupation vectors.
This approach addresses the fundamental nature of chemical reactions as transformations in electron space.

stories.title: Beyond F1: Evaluating Coverage and Failure Recovery in AI Model Security Scanners
stories.author: Indranil Sanyal
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in current AI model security scanner evaluations, which often only measure successful judgments.
The study benchmarks three existing scanners (ModelScan, ModelAudit, and Fickling) using a controlled, artifact-backed synthetic corpus.
The evaluation covers 170 Pickle and PyTorch artifacts across 145 specimen families, testing both known and intentional vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of outdated, fixed-variable sepsis severity indices in critical care.
Presents a novel approach to learning a continuous sepsis severity score directly from patient trajectories.
Validated through a retrospective study involving a large cohort across two hospital systems.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) internally structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs can distinguish between different Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models, one for each of the six MFT dimensions (e.g., care/harm, fairness).

stories.title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
stories.author: Rishikesan Kamaleswaran
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of outdated, fixed-variable sepsis severity indices.
A new model was developed to learn a continuous sepsis severity score directly from patient trajectories.
The study utilized a retrospective analysis across two large cohorts from different hospital systems.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: Research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs differentiate between specific Moral Foundations Theory (MFT) categories.
The methodology involves training linear probes on open-weight models to geometrically analyze the relationships between these moral foundations.

stories.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
stories.author: Wenguang Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost barrier in large language model (LLM) pretraining, a major hurdle for open-source and academic research.
Introduces 'Puro-2B,' a model trained using a consumer-grade GPU (RTX 5090) within a specified budget.
Contributes to the ongoing effort to create cost-efficient, hardware-accessible, and open-source LLM training recipes.

stories.title: Understanding Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning: Broader Reasoning Coverage than GRPO
stories.author: Zhenkun Wang
bullet_points: The paper investigates Evolution Strategies (ES) as a memory-efficient post-training method for LLM reasoning.
It systematically compares ES dynamics against mainstream methods like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO).
The research empirically and theoretically demonstrates a performance advantage of ES over GRPO in LLM reasoning tasks.

stories.title: Beyond Parallel Blindness: Information Floors and Model Gaps in Block Drafting
stories.author: Yufei Ding
bullet_points: The research addresses limitations in block drafting models by distinguishing between missing path information and imperfect observable modeling.
A novel concept, the 'information floor,' is introduced to quantify the minimum expected rejection rate under specific conditioning.
The 'model gap' is defined as the rejection rate exceeding this information floor, offering a new metric for model evaluation.

stories.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
stories.author: Ting Zhu
bullet_points: Introduces CritICL, a novel inference-time framework designed to improve LLM reasoning.
Addresses the inefficiency of current methods (like repeated generation) used to boost LLM performance.
Leverages the insight that LLM failure modes follow structured patterns across different scales within the same model family.

stories.title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
stories.author: Tu Vu
bullet_points: WikiSkill is a new framework designed to compile and persist specialized knowledge and workflows derived from AI agent experience.
It addresses the limitation where insights guiding skill development are currently scattered across optimization histories, hindering systematic reuse.
The system enables AI agents to progressively adapt and evolve their capabilities by making learned skills reusable resources.

stories.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of using large-scale agent trajectory datasets for fine-tuning LLMs on software issues.
The core problem identified is that successful trajectories can still contain noisy, redundant, or risky steps, leading to poor supervision.
SWE-Prime proposes a method to improve LLM performance by moving beyond simple supervised fine-tuning on raw successful trajectories.

stories.title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in advanced LLM post-training methods (like RL and OPSD) which require ground-truth labels.
It proposes Test-Time Policy Optimization (TTPO) to enable training during inference by using majority-vote pseudo-labels instead of ground truth.
The research highlights a critical fragility in pseudo-labeling methods, noting that incorrect votes can corrupt the model's learning process.

stories.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
stories.author: Zibin Zheng
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitation of current LLM-based code review systems, which treat the process as a single, static decision.
It introduces MCR-Bench to benchmark code review in a realistic, multi-round, and interactive manner.
The research aims to capture the complex, iterative problem-solving nature of real-world software development reviews.

stories.title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
stories.author: Dongyan Zhao
bullet_points: The paper addresses a key limitation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for LLMs: entropy collapse leading to narrow reasoning coverage.
The proposed method introduces cross-model non-parametric perturbation to actively preserve the generative diversity of LLMs during RLVR training.
This work offers an alternative to existing algorithmic regularizations, aiming to improve LLM performance metrics like pass@$k$ for large $k$.

stories.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge
stories.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) structure and organize moral knowledge.
The study moves beyond simple moral content detection to examine if LLMs distinguish between specific moral foundations (e.g., care/harm, fairness).
Researchers use linear probes trained on open-weight models to geometrically analyze the relationships between these moral foundations.

stories.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction
stories.author: Guanhua Chen
bullet_points: Clinical language models often fail in real-world deployment due to reliance on note-specific artifacts rather than true patient state.
The paper introduces CAST (Concept-guided Artifact Suppression Tuning), an SAE-based framework for improving clinical text classification.
CAST uses Sparse Autoencoders to extract human-auditable features from Transformer activations, enabling more robust and auditable models.

stories.title: The Most Important AI Agent Design Choice: Don’t Let the Model Be the Final Authority
stories.author: officialbidisha
bullet_points: The article discusses critical design principles for AI agents as they become more capable.
A key takeaway is the necessity of preventing the underlying AI model from being the sole decision-maker.
AI agents are noted for their growing abilities, including database querying and API interaction.
